play_info.title: The Lekki Headmaster
play_info.author: Kabir Alabi Garba
play_info.category: JAMB Use of English prescribed reading text

summary.overview: The Lekki Headmaster by Kabir Alabi Garba is a contemporary Nigerian novel set at Stardom Schools in Lekki, Lagos. It follows Bepo Adewale, a committed school headmaster whose professional life and loyalty to his students are tested when his family encourages him to relocate to the United Kingdom. Through school life, family relationships and the pressure to seek opportunities abroad, the novel explores education, leadership, migration, patriotism, responsibility and the meaning of service.
summary.plot_summary: Bepo Adewale has devoted many years to leading Stardom Schools in Lekki. His wife, Seri, and their daughters are living in the United Kingdom and want him to join them, while his responsibilities and relationships at school keep him closely connected to the students and community he serves. As he faces the prospect of leaving Nigeria for a different life abroad, events at the school and the experiences of people around him make him reflect on the value of his work, the challenges facing the education system and the consequences of migration. The central conflict is Bepo's decision between personal and family opportunities overseas and his commitment to the school and the young people who depend on him. The novel uses this conflict to examine the meaning of dedication, the pressures behind the desire to migrate, and the importance of responsible leadership.
